content: Gaviscon is an over-the-counter medication specifically designed for the treatment of heartburn and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), commonly referred to as acid reflux. It is manufactured and distributed in the United Kingdom by Reckitt Benckiser, while in the United States and Canada, it is produced and distributed by GlaxoSmithKline. The active antacid components in the Gaviscon formula available in the UK include aluminum hydroxide, combined with either magnesium carbonate or magnesium trisilicate. In addition to these acid-neutralizing agents, Gaviscon contains an alginate compound, which is a combination of alginic acid and sodium bicarbonate. When ingested, the interaction between alginic acid and sodium bicarbonate forms a protective barrier. This barrier functions to prevent stomach acid from refluxing into the esophagus. By doing so, it reduces the frequency of reflux episodes and provides relief from heartburn for up to four hours. In cases where reflux does occur, this protective barrier is the first substance to come into contact with the esophageal mucosa. As a result, it offers a layer of protection against the potentially harmful effects of gastric contents on the esophagus. For optimal management of GERD and heartburn, it may be beneficial to combine the use of Gaviscon with lifestyle modifications. These modifications can include weight loss, elevating the head of the bed during sleep, reducing alcohol consumption, and quitting smoking. Gaviscon operates in a non-systemic manner, meaning that its therapeutic effects are localized and the medication does not enter the bloodstream.
